mechanism_narrative: A restrictive-policy shock is visible when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall sharply in the same week; this suppresses commuting and discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will be lower than its prior 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week in the same week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -21.9 at t-1w to -29.4 at t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES fell from -8.3 at t-1w to -37.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its prior 28-day mean despite the joint TRANSIT and WORKPLACES threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: A jump in RESIDENTIAL mobility means more people are staying home, which reduces trips to retail-and-recreation venues; when RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 percent, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days will be lower than its prior 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than its prior 28-day mean when RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 percent change.
